title: The First Marquis Bleeds
text:
Qin Luo — the **Silent Bell**, then World Rank #6 — was the strongest active Marquis of his generation, using vibration rather than ordinary sight to read movement through terrain and bodies.

Qin Luo was attacked at dawn.

Qin Luo was World Rank #6 — the Silent Bell, strongest of the current Marquises. Back in the earlier conflicts around Sera, Qin had already crossed paths with her as an old rival. His vibration sense could read movement without relying on ordinary sight, and few among the Top Ten could hide their approach from him. This time, however, someone had come specifically prepared to hunt the Silent Bell.

The Black Banner did not send assassins.

They sent a battlefield.

Three hundred fighters occupied a mountain pass, forcing Qin to fight while civilians were trapped behind him.

Qin understood immediately.

This was not an attempt to defeat him.

It was a study.

A voice came from the ridge.

The voice belonged to Yan Luochen — the Black Banner. He was a former Western Campaign commander, not a current ranked fighter, whose danger came from turning battlefields into experiments. He studied how strong people behaved under pressure, then built the next battlefield around those habits.

[[speaker:yan]]“World Rank #6. The Silent Bell.”

A tall man stepped into view.

His black military coat was faded, not decorative. His hands carried old scars.

[[speaker:yan]]“Yan Luochen.”

Qin recognized the name.

Former Western Campaign commander.

A man who had once commanded armies larger than some kingdoms.

[[speaker:qin]]“You're not strong enough to beat me.”

Yan smiled.

The pass exploded into motion.

Qin realized the battlefield had been designed to make him reveal priorities, not techniques. Every civilian placement, collapsing wagon and hidden archer forced a choice. He began answering those choices incorrectly on purpose. Instead of pursuing Yan's retreat, he struck the road and listened to the vibration returning through the mountain. Three concealed anchor points answered.

[[speaker:qin]]“You are measuring me.”

Yan did not deny it.

[[speaker:yan]]“Everyone measures legends. I prefer useful measurements.”

Qin's expression hardened. He sent one vibration through the pass, enough to collapse the formation's timing without touching the trapped families. Yan withdrew before the fight could become a straightforward contest. That was how Qin knew the encounter had never been intended as one.

Hours later, Sera received Qin's report at the tea shop. Rhen reached for the page. She moved it away.

[[speaker:sera]]“Mine first.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Possessive.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Efficient.”

She read every line twice. By the time she finished, the pattern had begun forming in her head.

The aftermath of Qin's ambush took most of the day.

He personally walked the trapped families out of the pass before allowing anyone to examine his injuries. That detail mattered to Sera when she later reconstructed Yan's model. The Black Banner had not simply recorded Qin's technique range. It had recorded the exact point at which duty overrode pursuit.

Sera wrote one note beside his name:

HE WILL ALWAYS TURN BACK FOR PEOPLE.

Then she crossed it out.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Why remove it?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Because that's not a weakness.”

She underlined the sentence instead.

[[speaker:sera]]“It's a choice.”

The distinction became the foundation of her counter-strategy.

That night Qin finally reached Sera's tea shop.

He set one broken Black Banner token on the counter.

No greeting.

No complaint.

Sera looked at the fracture running through the metal.

[[speaker:sera]]“How bad?”

Qin lowered himself into the chair opposite her.

[[speaker:qin]]“He knew what I would do before I did it.”

Rhen's eyes sharpened.

Sera picked up the token.

On its underside, etched so finely that only an assassin would bother checking, were six characters.

SILENT BELL — RESPONSE CONFIRMED.

Sera's expression changed.

This was not reconnaissance anymore.

Someone had begun building answers to the Top Ten.

Outside, rain struck the windows.

Qin looked toward Rhen.

[[speaker:qin]]“If this man finishes studying us, what happens?”

Rhen answered quietly.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Then the next battlefield won't be designed to beat your techniques.”

Sera turned the token over in her fingers.

[[speaker:rhen]]“It will be designed to beat you.”

title: The Black Banner
text:
Yan's strategy became clear.

He had studied every current Marquis.

Not to overpower them.

To force them into situations where their greatest strengths became liabilities.

Arin was next.

Kael Veyran was still **World Rank #1, Duke of the Unmoving Heaven**. More importantly, he was among the handful of living fighters who had personally experienced the impossible gap between the public rankings and Rhen.

Arin Vale was World Rank #9 — the Silver Sword Saint and Kael Veyran's only direct disciple. Arin had fought alongside Qin before, carrying the discipline Kael Veyran had drilled into his only direct disciple. She was never defined by raw destruction; her danger lay in precision, timing and an uncanny ability to find the seam in almost anything.

She found herself fighting inside a ruined monastery where every sword stroke risked collapsing the roof onto civilians.

She stopped using wide techniques.

Yan's men had expected exactly that.

[[speaker:arin]]“You studied my sword.”

She drew a smaller blade.

[[speaker:arin]]“You didn't study me.”

She broke the formation.

Arin's monastery battle lasted far longer than the first exchange suggested. The Black Banner had studied her sweeping arcs, counter timing and preference for structural seams. So Arin stopped fighting like the Silver Sword Saint people wrote about.

She shortened her grip, changed stance, and used a broken prayer board as an off-hand shield. Every adjustment made the enemy's prepared answers less useful. When one swordsman tried to collapse the roof onto refugees, Arin cut only the three joints carrying the weight and redirected the fall harmlessly into an empty corridor.

Arin turned the smaller blade in her hand.

[[speaker:arin]]“Your notes ended where improvisation began.”

Later, Sera read the field report and smiled.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You approve.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Very much.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Should I be jealous?”

Sera looked at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“Of Arin?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You smiled.”

She leaned over and kissed his cheek.

[[speaker:sera]]“There. Balanced.”

Rhen went silent. Sera returned to the report as though nothing had happened.

Arin remained at the monastery after the fighting ended.

She helped repair the roof herself.

One novice asked why a Top Ten swordswoman was carrying timber.

Arin answered simply:

[[speaker:arin]]“Because I broke part of it.”

That story reached Sera before the formal combat report did.

Sera smiled when she heard it.

Yan Luochen had spent weeks studying the Silver Sword Saint.

He had not understood the woman who would stay until midnight fixing a roof after winning.

That human inconsistency was exactly what Sera intended to weaponize.

Arin returned to the monastery courtyard after midnight.

The refugees were asleep.

The Black Banner soldiers were gone.

One prayer board remained hanging crooked beneath the repaired roof.

Arin reached up and straightened it.

A novice approached carrying a folded strip of black cloth found among the enemy supplies.

[[speaker:novice]]“Sword Saint.”

Arin took it.

Unlike Qin's token, this one carried no confirmed response.

Only a question.

SILVER SWORD SAINT — SECONDARY STYLE UNKNOWN.

Arin stared at the line.

Not warmly.

She drew the smaller blade she had used inside the monastery and cut the cloth cleanly in half.

The novice blinked.

[[speaker:novice]]“Good?”

Arin sheathed the blade.

[[speaker:arin]]“Let him keep wondering.”

Far away, Yan Luochen received the incomplete report.

For the first time since beginning the Marquis campaign, the Black Banner crossed out one of his own predictions.

Under Arin Vale's name, he wrote a single word.

ADAPTIVE.

Then he turned the page.

The next name waiting for him was Han Myeong.

World Rank #8.

The Ashen Beast.

title: Sera Reads the Pattern
text:
Sera noticed something neither Marquis had.

Every battlefield contained the same geometric error.

A deliberate weakness.

[[speaker:sera]]“He's teaching them.”

Rhen looked at the map.

[[speaker:sera]]“They're learning how the Marquises respond under pressure.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“And then?”

[[speaker:sera]]“They're going to make the Marquises fight one another.”

She looked at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“Which means you're coming with me.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Where?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Dinner.”

He blinked.

[[speaker:sera]]“We can investigate after.”

Sera covered three tea-shop tables with maps, witness statements and recovered Black Banner notes. Rhen attempted to relocate one teapot. She slapped his hand away.

[[speaker:sera]]“Evidence.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Tea.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Evidence first.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“This shop has standards.”

[[speaker:sera]]“I own the standards.”

The key was not where the attacks happened but what each Marquis had been forced to do. Qin defended before pursuing. Arin compressed her sword style. Han escalated endurance. Luo Wen abandoned offense the moment wounded civilians appeared.

Sera moved four markers.

The geometry became obvious.

[[speaker:sera]]“Yan isn't trying to defeat them yet.”

[[speaker:sera]]“He wants their decisions.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“And once he has them?”

[[speaker:sera]]“He'll build a battlefield where every Marquis behaves exactly as expected.”

Rhen watched her for a moment.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You are very attractive when you're terrifying.”

Sera stopped moving markers.

[[speaker:sera]]“You cannot say that while I'm working.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Noted.”

He was smiling. She hated that her ears felt warm.

Rhen eventually gave up trying to rescue the teapot from Sera's evidence table.

Instead he sat beside her.

Not across.

Beside.

Sera noticed.

[[speaker:sera]]“Copying me now?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Learning.”

She moved one map closer so they could both see it.

Their shoulders remained touching while they worked.

The mystery became intimate in the quietest possible way: shared paper, shared tea, and Rhen trusting Sera enough not to provide the answer before she found it herself.

When Sera finally circled Yan's likely command route, Rhen nodded.

[[speaker:rhen]]“I agree.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You sound surprised.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Impressed.”

She pretended that word did not affect her.

Sera drew one final line across the map.

It connected Qin's pass, Arin's monastery, and the mine district Han had not yet reached.

At the center sat an empty circle.

No location.

A prediction.

[[speaker:sera]]“He's building toward someone.”

Rhen looked at the circle.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Who?”

Sera wrote one name inside it.

HAN MYEONG.

Then she underlined it twice.

title: A Dinner Before War
text:
Sera chose a quiet restaurant.

She deliberately sat beside Rhen.

Not across.

Beside.

He looked at her.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You're doing this deliberately.”

She took his hand under the table.

[[speaker:sera]]“Because I can.”

Rhen squeezed her fingers.

She smiled into her tea.

The moment lasted exactly eleven seconds before a messenger arrived bleeding.

Sera sighed.

[[speaker:sera]]“I hate our timing.”

The restaurant was small enough that nobody recognized them. Sera had chosen it for exactly that reason.

No Dukes. No Marquises. No frozen petals.

Just dinner.

Rhen read the menu with the concentration of a man studying an assassination manual.

[[speaker:sera]]“You are nervous.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You have fought armies.”

[[speaker:sera]]“But dinner is difficult.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Different skill set.”

Sera laughed, then slid her hand beneath the table and took his.

Rhen froze for half a breath.

Then his fingers closed around hers.

The gesture was so simple that it affected her more than half the dramatic things he had done over the years.

[[speaker:sera]]“You could have done that sooner.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I wasn't sure you wanted me to.”

Sera's expression softened.

[[speaker:sera]]“I do.”

The messenger arrived seconds later, bleeding through one sleeve.

Sera sighed.

[[speaker:sera]]“Our timing remains terrible.”

Rhen stood, but neither of them let go until the messenger reached the table.

After the wounded messenger interrupted dinner, Sera stood reluctantly.

Rhen paid before following.

Outside, she realized he still held her hand.

Neither had noticed.

Sera looked down.

[[speaker:sera]]“You can let go.”

Rhen started to.

Her fingers tightened.

[[speaker:sera]]“I said can.”

Sera smiled despite the blood on the messenger's sleeve.

[[speaker:sera]]“Come on.”

They ran through the city still holding hands for the first half of the street.

Only then did duty finally separate them.

The messenger's report named the next battlefield.

An abandoned mining district.

Sera's expression changed immediately.

[[speaker:sera]]“Han.”

Rhen stood.

Their unfinished dinner remained on the table behind them.

Sera glanced back once.

[[speaker:sera]]“We're coming back.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“To the restaurant?”

She took his hand again.

[[speaker:sera]]“To the date.”

Then they ran.

title: #8 Against the Black Banner
text:
Han Myeong fought Yan directly.

Han Myeong was World Rank #8 — the Ashen Beast, a body-cultivation monster whose furnace qi, durability and attrition fighting made him one of the hardest current Marquises to stop once he committed to close combat.

The battle lasted twenty minutes.

Han's furnace gauntlets shattered three Black Banner weapons.

Yan survived every exchange by refusing to fight where Han was strongest.

Han eventually forced him into close quarters.

Yan laughed.

[[speaker:yan]]“There you are.”

Han understood.

Yan had wanted to see the full Ashen Beast system.

He escaped before Han could finish him.

Han was furious.

Han and Yan's direct battle unfolded inside an abandoned mining district, where narrow shafts and metal rails turned every burst of furnace qi into a potential trap. Yan had prepared the terrain for days. Han understood that within minutes.

That did not make him cautious.

It made him angry.

The Ashen Beast forced close quarters anyway. Furnace pressure warped iron supports. Yan redirected, retreated, and repeatedly baited Han into revealing how he handled sustained heat in enclosed space.

[[speaker:han]]“You really are studying us.”

Han smiled without humor.

[[speaker:han]]“Then take notes.”

The next exchange destroyed the mine entrance.

Yan escaped through a tunnel he had prepared in advance. Han emerged through the dust with one burned arm and a new understanding of the enemy.

He had not lost.

But Yan had gotten what he wanted.

Back at the temporary camp, Sera wrapped Han's arm herself while questioning him.

[[speaker:han]]“Your physician looks unhappy.”

[[speaker:sera]]“He's not my physician.”

Rhen raised an eyebrow.

Sera kept wrapping.

[[speaker:sera]]“He's my problem.”

Han decided not to ask.

Han spent the evening replaying his fight.

Not the strikes.

The choices.

Yan had forced him to decide between chasing the commander and stabilizing a collapsing shaft where miners had been hidden.

Han chose the miners.

Of course he did.

That choice appeared in the Black Banner's records as PREDICTABLE DIVERSION RESPONSE.

Han nearly tore the page in half.

Sera stopped him.

[[speaker:sera]]“Keep it.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Because eventually you'll enjoy proving it wrong.”

Han stared at her.

Then folded the page carefully.

Rhen watched the exchange.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You collect difficult people.”

Sera glanced at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“You included.”

Han returned from the mine with one burned arm and a torn Black Banner map.

He dropped it in front of Sera.

Only one route remained unmarked.

A road leading directly toward the Marquis gathering point.

[[speaker:han]]“He's done studying individually.”

Sera unfolded the map.

Han stared.

[[speaker:han]]“Good?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Now he thinks he understands all of you.”

title: The Marquis Assembly
text:
For the first time, several current Marquises naturally converged.

#6 Qin.

#8 Han.

#9 Arin.

#10 Luo Wen.

Sera arrived last.

No one summoned her.

She came because she had already solved the strategic problem.

[[speaker:sera]]“You're all fighting him separately.”

Qin stared.

[[speaker:qin]]“You have a better plan?”

She placed the map down.

Rhen stood behind her.

Nobody asked why.

The Marquis meeting was tense because nobody enjoyed admitting Sera had solved the strategic pattern first.

Qin stood over the map. Han leaned against a pillar with his injured arm wrapped. Arin sat with her sword across her knees. Luo Wen had already checked everyone's pulse

Luo Wen was World Rank #10, known as the Grave Physician. He combined anatomy, acupoints, disabling strikes and healing knowledge, making him one of the least flashy but most technically dangerous people in the Top Ten. and declared martial pride a chronic medical condition.

Sera arrived carrying tea.

[[speaker:sera]]“Drink.”

[[speaker:qin]]“Is that part of the plan?”

[[speaker:han]]“How?”

[[speaker:sera]]“You're less irritating when hydrated.”

Arin looked away to hide a smile.

Rhen remained near the doorway and did not take command. The strategy belonged to Sera.

Her solution was counterintuitive: the Marquises would stop behaving like their legends. Qin would appear reckless. Han cautious. Arin obvious. Luo aggressive. Sera predictable.

[[speaker:qin]]“You want us to fight incorrectly.”

[[speaker:sera]]“I want you to fight like people instead of reputations.”

Silence followed.

Then Qin nodded.

That was the moment the Marquis War changed.

The meeting continued long after the tea went cold.

Each Marquis objected to Sera's plan for a different reason.

That helped.

Qin disliked deliberate recklessness.

Han disliked restraint.

Arin disliked obvious movement.

Luo Wen disliked being asked to attack at all.

Sera listened to every complaint.

Then adjusted the plan around them instead of forcing everyone into one style.

That was the difference between her strategy and Yan's.

Yan wanted people predictable enough to model.

Sera wanted them free enough to surprise him.

By midnight, even Qin admitted the plan might work.

Sera leaned back.

[[speaker:sera]]“Might?”

[[speaker:qin]]“I am being generous.”

Rhen quietly placed fresh tea beside her.

She took it without looking.

That small familiarity did not escape Arin's notice.

When the meeting ended, nobody left by the route assigned to them.

That was deliberate.

Qin departed through the kitchen.

Han climbed a wall.

Arin borrowed Luo Wen's cloak.

Luo Wen simply walked out the front door because everyone assumed he would do something clever.

Sera watched them scatter.

Rhen stood beside her.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Your army is strange.”

[[speaker:sera]]“They're not my army.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You say that like they didn't just follow your plan.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Five roads.”

title: Five Roads
text:
The Marquises split.

Each took a different road.

The Black Banner expected them to coordinate.

They didn't.

Instead Sera deliberately fed Yan false information.

Arin attacked the wrong supply line.

Han destroyed a bridge.

Qin waited.

Luo disappeared.

The battlefield became unreadable.

Yan finally realized who had changed the rules.

[[speaker:yan]]“The Pale Orchid.”

Sera smiled from the ridge.

[[speaker:sera]]“Took you long enough.”

Five roads opened before dawn, each carrying false intent.

Arin attacked a supply depot but left the command seals untouched. Han destroyed a bridge after making certain Black Banner scouts saw him choose the 'wrong' side. Qin spent six hours doing nothing, which unnerved Yan more than any assault. Luo Wen prepared a visible medical camp full of harmless dye and let enemy observers report poison.

Sera made herself easiest to follow.

Her route, clothes, inn and apparent objective were all visible.

Then she disappeared through a kitchen before midnight and entered Yan's information network instead.

By morning the Black Banner had six contradictory versions of the Marquis plan.

Yan read the reports.

PALE ORCHID SIGHTED IN THREE LOCATIONS.

He stared at that line longer than the rest.

[[speaker:yan]]“She isn't hiding from us.”

His lieutenant frowned.

[[speaker:yan]]“She's teaching us not to trust what we know.”

At the tea shop far away, Rhen sneezed.

Sera's old assistant asked why.

Rhen looked toward the horizon.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Someone is probably regretting underestimating her.”

The false-road operation became more complicated when Yan began feeding false information back.

Sera expected that.

She planted two reports she wanted him to 'discover' and allowed one to be genuinely correct.

The correct report was the trap.

Yan believed Sera would never risk truth inside a deception network.

She absolutely would.

When his reserve force moved to intercept the real route, Qin was already waiting in silence.

No giant technique.

No announcement.

Just the Silent Bell standing in the road.

The reserve turned around.

Sera received the signal minutes later.

Rhen looked over.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Satisfied?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Very.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Dangerous expression.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You like it.”

Rhen did not deny that.

Yan received the sixth contradictory report just before dawn.

He placed it beside the other five.

For the first time, none of his predictions agreed with one another.

His lieutenant asked which report was false.

Yan looked at all six.

[[speaker:yan]]“That is the problem.”

Far away, Sera extinguished a lantern.

One road remained.

The one Yan would choose himself.

title: The Black Banner Falls
text:
Yan finally confronted Sera.

He was stronger.

She was faster.

He had more endurance.

She had already mapped his decision-making.

The fight became psychological.

Sera won.

Not because she was stronger.

Because she knew when he would choose to retreat.

Her blade stopped at his throat.

[[speaker:sera]]“You wanted to understand the Marquises.”

Yan stared.

[[speaker:sera]]“Now understand this.”

She lowered the blade.

[[speaker:sera]]“We're people.”

Sera confronted Yan alone inside a burned command hall.

He was stronger.

She knew it.

He knew she knew it.

[[speaker:yan]]“And you came anyway.”

[[speaker:sera]]“I do that.”

The fight lasted longer than either expected. Yan's force shattered pillars. Sera refused every direct contest. She attacked his rhythm, retreat habits and assumptions.

One strike grazed her ribs because she had deliberately allowed the opening. Yan committed to the follow-up he had used twelve times in previous reports.

Silken Grave caught the rear beam.

The roof shifted.

Not enough to collapse.

Enough to remove his preferred escape angle.

For the first time since the Black Banner arrived, Yan had no prepared route.

Sera's blade stopped at his throat.

Yan breathed hard beneath the blade.

[[speaker:sera]]“Your profiles were never the problem.”

She lowered the weapon.

[[speaker:sera]]“Believing they were complete was.”

Yan surrendered.

Not because Sera overpowered a Duke-level commander.

Because she defeated the system he used to understand everyone else.

Yan's surrender did not make Sera relax.

She questioned him for hours.

Not about techniques.

About motives.

He admitted the Black Banner began after watching ranked masters destroy armies while ordinary soldiers were expected to understand none of the rules governing them.

He wanted a world where legends could be studied, predicted and countered.

Sera understood the fear.

She rejected the conclusion.

[[speaker:sera]]“Understanding people is not the same as reducing them.”

Yan looked toward the doorway where Rhen waited.

[[speaker:yan]]“Easy to say when that man chooses your side.”

Sera's expression cooled.

[[speaker:sera]]“He chose himself.”

[[speaker:sera]]“He just happens to stay with me.”

Rhen heard that.

He looked away so she would not see him smile.

Yan surrendered his weapon.

Sera did not celebrate.

She searched his coat.

Inside was a final folded page.

Not a Marquis profile.

Her own.

PALE ORCHID.

VARIABLE RESPONSE.

PREDICTION RELIABILITY: UNACCEPTABLE.

Sera read it twice.

Then laughed.

She folded the page and put it in her pocket.

[[speaker:sera]]“Best compliment I've had all week.”

title: Rhen's Quiet Compliment
text:
Afterward, Rhen found Sera alone.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You were impressive.”

She looked at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“That's all?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Very impressive.”

She stepped closer.

[[speaker:sera]]“Better.”

Then she fixed his collar.

[[speaker:sera]]“You're learning.”

He smiled.

Rhen found Sera after the healers finished wrapping her ribs.

She was sitting outside, watching rain collect on the roof tiles.

He sat beside her.

Said nothing.

[[speaker:sera]]“You're doing the quiet thing.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You were injured.”

[[speaker:sera]]“I noticed.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I wanted to interfere.”

Sera turned toward him.

That admission mattered.

[[speaker:sera]]“But you didn't.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You asked me not to.”

She leaned against his shoulder.

Rhen exhaled.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You are becoming increasingly difficult to protect.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Excellent.”

She looked up.

[[speaker:sera]]“I don't want you deciding when I need protection.”

[[speaker:sera]]“I want you trusting me.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I do.”

Sera kissed his cheek.

[[speaker:sera]]“Much better.”

This time, Rhen turned his head quickly enough that her lips nearly caught the corner of his mouth.

Both froze.

Sera smiled first.

[[speaker:sera]]“Interesting.”

Rhen looked suddenly less composed than he had against armies.

That night Sera woke because her ribs hurt.

Rhen was still sitting beside the bed.

[[speaker:sera]]“You haven't slept.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Neither have you.”

[[speaker:sera]]“I'm injured. I have an excuse.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I am worried. I have one too.”

Sera went quiet.

Then lifted the blanket.

[[speaker:sera]]“Come here.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Not like that. Sit.”

He sat on the edge.

Sera leaned against him.

[[speaker:sera]]“Better.”

Rhen remained motionless until she whispered:

[[speaker:sera]]“You can breathe.”

He laughed softly.

When Sera finally stood to return inside, pain caught her ribs.

Rhen's hand appeared at her elbow.

She allowed it.

Only for a moment.

At the doorway she stopped.

She kissed the corner of his mouth.

Quickly.

Deliberately.

Then walked inside.

Rhen remained outside for several seconds.

For once, the hidden legend had absolutely no idea what to do next.

title: The Banner Burns
text:
The Black Banner dissolved.

Yan disappeared.

The Marquises returned to their territories.

No Duke needed to appear.

The Marquises had solved a Duke-level strategic threat themselves.

At the tea shop, Sera rested her head against Rhen.

[[speaker:sera]]“I think I'm getting used to this.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“To what?”

[[speaker:sera]]“You.”

He was quiet.

[[speaker:sera]]“Don't look so frightened.”

The Black Banner did not disappear overnight. Sera insisted the surrendered fighters be separated from the doctrine that had trained them to see ranked martial artists as predictable systems.

Qin returned home with new training methods.

Han kept the scar from the mine.

Arin pinned Yan's report describing her as predictable above her training wall.

Luo Wen ordered everyone to rest and was ignored.

At the tea shop, Sera finally obeyed.

She fell asleep at the table.

Rhen found her there and draped a blanket over her shoulders.

Her eyes opened slightly.

[[speaker:sera]]“You don't have to.”

He stopped.

The phrase echoed an older moment.

Sera's expression softened.

She reached out beneath the blanket and found his hand.

[[speaker:sera]]“Stay.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I was planning to.”

Sera closed her eyes.

The Marquis War ended without a grand assembly or another Duke arriving to solve it.

The Marquises had won.

Sera had led the strategy.

And Rhen had learned, slowly, that standing beside her sometimes meant doing nothing until she asked.

The final night after the Black Banner surrendered was almost peaceful.

No alarms.

No messengers.

No ancient sovereigns.

Sera cooked badly.

Rhen ate everything anyway.

[[speaker:sera]]“You don't have to pretend.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I'm not.”

She tasted the food herself and made a face.

[[speaker:sera]]“Liar.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I have survived worse.”

Sera threw a cloth at him.

Later they sat outside under the eaves.

Her head found his shoulder automatically.

Rhen rested his cheek lightly against her hair.

Neither commented.

Their closeness was becoming ordinary.

For two people who had spent years treating attachment like danger, ordinary was enormous.

The next morning, the Black Banner files were sealed.

Sera placed Yan's profile of her at the bottom of the cabinet.

VARIABLE RESPONSE.
